newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone journalists face spying charges.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone journalists face spying charges.

text.p: Three journalists working for an independent newspaper in Sierra Leone have been charged with spying for rebels -- a charge that can carry the death penalty, justice officials said on Saturday.

The three, editor-in-chief Ibrahim Sheaga Shaw, Gibril Koroma and Abayomi Charles Roberts of the thrice-weekly Expo Times, pleaded not guilty before a magistrates court on Friday and were remanded in custody until Monday.
The prosecution accused them of obtaining secret official documents that could be of use to the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), which took up arms in 1991.

Police arrested the three on Wednesday after Expo Times published a story accusing Nigeria's military leader, Sani Abacha, of detaining RUF founder Foday Sankoh so other members of the RUF leadership could oust him as leader.
It headlined the piece "Abacha's wild west gangsterism".
Members of the RUF high command said last weekend that they had sacked Sankoh, who is under arrest in Nigeria, for blocking the peace process.
Sierra Leone, rich in diamonds and other minerals, is one of the world's poorest nations.
Sankoh signed a peace deal with President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah in Ivory Coast on November 30. Implementation has dragged, suggesting that the deal was unravelling.
Tejan Kabbah took office a year ago after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule.
